title: Explainable Authorization Catalog: RBAC v2 role model and permission resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As part of the RBAC v2 initiative we need a role model that is both machine-efficient for fast permission checks in the inference runtime and explainable for audit and admin workflows. Current role artifacts are ad-hoc and hard to reason about for support engineers and auditors.

Objective: Produce an authorization catalog and resolution flow that maps: resource hierarchy (resource types and tenancy boundaries) -> scopes (operation-level and context-scoped) -> grants (allow/deny, temporal) -> derived effective permissions. The catalog must support explainability (human-readable grant provenance), efficient evaluation (O(1) or O(log N) common-case checks), and auditability (linkable events for SSO/SAML sign-ins and privileged operations).

Scope: This ticket covers the canonical role/resource model, permission matrix examples, APIs for explainable permission lookups, and an export format for console display and audit trails. Implementation of runtime enforcement will be a follow-up ticket.

Proposal summary:
- Resource ontology: define canonical resource types (organization, tenant, project, model, route, deployment, capacity-pool) and allowed parent relationships. Include tenancy boundary rules (global vs tenant-scoped vs resource-scoped).
- Scope categories: management (create/update/delete), runtime (invoke/stream), observation (read/metrics/logs), admin (billing, policies). Each scope gets an adjective: "read", "write", "manage", "admin".
- Role primitives: base-role (set of grants), role-templates (composable across tenants), temporal-exceptions (break-glass with expiration), implicit-service-roles (for system agents).
- Permission matrix: provide a matrix mapping (resource type X scope) -> minimal grants required for common personas (engineer, platform-admin, billing, support). Include explicit deny precedence rules and inheritance semantics.
- Explainability: every effective permission lookup must return provenance: direct grants, inherited grants, time-bounded overrides, and MR (matching rule) id. The MR id links to a human-readable rule stored in the catalog and to audit logs for the decision event.
- APIs: GET /auth/explain?principal=...&resource=...&action=... returns a structured explanation (but serialized as a compact string/array for the catalog export).

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Trade-off between a fully normalized graph (easy to audit) vs denormalized cache for speed. We propose a hybrid: keep authoritative graph in the catalog store, generate denormalized evaluation-ready blobs for hot principals and cache with TTL tied to role changes.
- Deny-first semantics simplifies security reasoning but complicates inheritance; we'll adopt explicit deny precedence with a clear bulk migration plan to mark legacy implicit denies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canonical resource ontology documented in the catalog (CSV + Markdown) covering all production resource types.
- Proof-of-concept explain endpoint design and sample payloads for 5 persona scenarios.
- Permission matrix populated for top 12 operations across resource types.
- Design reviewed by Security and Platform (comments addressed).

Open questions:
1) How do we represent compound scopes (e.g., "invoke:streaming") for streaming tokens and KV cache spikes?
2) What is the TTL target for denormalized evaluation blobs to balance freshness vs cost?
3) How do we surface temporary break-glass events in the Console timeline and in audit exports?

References and links: Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood/team/rbac-v2/catalog-proposal (internal). Design slide deck: https://drive.redwood/team/rbac-v2/explainable-catalog-slides. Existing migration notes: GH issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/5201.

Notes on compliance: The explainable output must include non-repudiable links to audit events (timestamp, actor, session-id) to satisfy enterprise audit requests.
